# Sources

Data retrieved: **2026-09-13**

All figures come from the U.S. Census Bureau's **American Community Survey (ACS) 1-year estimates**, as compiled into the Bureau's pre-built "Health Insurance Historical Tables" (no API key required — these are static files, not API calls). Only the **United States** (national) rows were used; state rows in each file were ignored.

## Files downloaded

| File | Table | Universe | Coverage | URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hic04_acs.xlsx` | HIC-4_ACS | All persons | 2008–2024 | https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/demo/tables/health-insurance/time-series/acs/hic04_acs.xlsx |
| `hic05_acs.xlsx` | HIC-5_ACS | Children under 19 | 2008–2024 | https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/demo/tables/health-insurance/time-series/acs/hic05_acs.xlsx |
| `hic06_acs.xlsx` | HIC-6_ACS | Persons under 65 | 2008–2024 | https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/demo/tables/health-insurance/time-series/acs/hic06_acs.xlsx |

Index page listing these files: https://www.census.gov/data/tables/time-series/demo/health-insurance/historical-series/hic.html

Each file is a single continuously-updated workbook (one "United States" row per file, one 4-column block of `Estimate / Margin of error / Percent / Margin of error` per year, 2008–2024). Before combining any years or files, the "United States" row block (Total → .Any coverage → .Uninsured) was checked in every file and confirmed to sit at the same row offset and use the same population definition ("Children under 19", "Persons under 65", "All persons") across all 17 year-columns within that file — i.e., no table silently changed its age cutoff partway through its own time series. 2020 is blank in all three source files (ACS did not release standard 2020 1-year estimates because of COVID-19 data-collection disruptions) and is therefore **omitted from the CSV entirely**, as instructed.

## How each age_group was derived

The three source tables give three overlapping, nested populations: **All persons** ⊃ **Persons under 65** ⊃ **Children under 19**. `uninsured_by_age.csv` reshapes these into three non-overlapping groups: `Under 19`, `19 to 64`, `65 and over`.

- **`Under 19`** — taken directly from HIC-5_ACS's "United States / .Uninsured" row (Percent + Margin of error). No arithmetic.

- **`19 to 64`** — derived as (Persons under 65) minus (Children under 19), since Under 65 = Under 19 + 19-to-64:
  - `total_19_64 = total_under65 − total_under19`
  - `uninsured_19_64 = uninsured_under65 − uninsured_under19`
  - `pct_uninsured = uninsured_19_64 / total_19_64 × 100`

- **`65 and over`** — derived as (All persons) minus (Persons under 65), since All = Under 65 + 65-and-over:
  - `total_65plus = total_all − total_under65`
  - `uninsured_65plus = uninsured_all − uninsured_under65`
  - `pct_uninsured = uninsured_65plus / total_65plus × 100`

## How margin_of_error was derived

For `Under 19`, the margin of error is the one Census already published for that row.

For the two derived groups (`19 to 64` and `65 and over`), margins of error were propagated from the published margins of error of the two source estimates using the standard Census ACS formulas (see the *ACS Accuracy of the Data* documentation footnoted in each source file, e.g. https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/ACS_Accuracy_of_Data_2024.pdf):

1. **Difference of two counts** (used for both the derived numerator and the derived denominator):
   `MOE(A − B) = sqrt(MOE_A² + MOE_B²)`
   This is the Census-recommended default when the covariance between the two estimates is not published (it is a conservative approximation).

2. **Percentage where the numerator is a subset of the denominator** (used to turn the derived uninsured count and derived population count into a percent + MOE):
   `SE(p) = sqrt(SE_num² − p² × SE_den²) / denominator`, falling back to `sqrt(SE_num² + p² × SE_den²) / denominator` if the first expression is negative, where `SE = MOE / 1.645` and `p` is the proportion uninsured. The result is converted back to a margin of error by multiplying by 1.645 and by 100 (to express it in percentage points).

Caveat: because the `65 and over` group is a small residual left after subtracting two much larger, highly correlated national totals, its relative margin of error is wider than a directly-published ACS estimate for the same group would be (most visible in 2008–2013, where the derived MOE is nearly as large as the estimate itself). Treat `65 and over` estimates as approximate; if tighter precision is needed for that group, request a Census API key and pull ACS Subject Table **S2701** (variable `S2701_C05_013E`, "Percent Uninsured, 65 years and older"), which publishes a directly-estimated MOE for that exact age band instead of a derived one.

## Column definitions (`uninsured_by_age.csv`)

- `year` — calendar year of the ACS 1-year estimate (2008–2024, 2020 omitted)
- `age_group` — one of `Under 19`, `19 to 64`, `65 and over`
- `pct_uninsured` — percent of the civilian noninstitutionalized population in that age group with no health insurance coverage
- `margin_of_error` — margin of error on `pct_uninsured`, in percentage points, at the 90% confidence level (Census ACS default)

164	
165	## Chart chrome & ink
166	
167	| Role | Light | Dark |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
170	| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
171	| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#ffffff` |
172	| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
173	| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
174	| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
175	| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
176	| Delta up good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
177	| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |
178	
179	## Filter controls
180	
181	Filters are standard UI, not chart components - the chart layer only adds the
182	composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
183	rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
184	bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
185	footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.
186	
187	## Typeface & figures
188	
189	Everything - including the hero figure - stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
190	-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
191	standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
192	figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
193	vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.
194

1	# Marks & anatomy
2	
3	The quiet, considered look is a few fixed specs plus two pieces of negative space.
4	The data is the only thing allowed to be loud.
5	
6	## Mark specs (fixed across every chart)
7	
8	| Mark | Spec |
9	|---|---|
10	| Bar / column | **<= 24px thick** (cap it - never fill the slot; let the band's leftover be air); **4px rounded data-end, square at the baseline**; grows from a single baseline |
11	| Line | **2px**, round join/cap |
12	| Marker / end-dot | **>= 8px** (r >= 4), filled with the series color |
13	| Area fill | the series hue at **~10% opacity** (a wash, never a saturated block) |
14	| Gridlines / axes | one-step-off-surface gray, **hairline (1px), solid** (never dashed), recessive |
15	
16	## The two spacers (white doing the separating)
17	
18	- **Surface gap.** A **2px gap** in the surface color separates touching marks - every
19	  segment of a stacked bar, and every adjacent (touching) bar, the same width. Keep it
20	  one consistent width across a stack; neighbors one step apart read distinct because of
21	  the gap, not a stroke drawn around them.
22	- **Surface ring.** Dots and end-markers carry a **2px ring in the surface color**,
23	  so they stay legible where they cross a line or overlap each other. The ring is part
24	  of the mark's hover/hit target, not just spacing - see `interaction.md` (small dots
25	  are easy to under-size for hover).
26	
27	Never draw a border around a mark to separate it. The gap and the ring are the
28	mechanism; a stroke adds data-weight ink that isn't data.
29	
30	## Labels & legend
31	
32	A **legend is always present for two or more series** - the dependable identity
33	channel; never make the reader rely on color-matching alone. Direct labels then ride
34	the marks to *supplement* it. **A single series needs no legend box**: there is only
35	one color, so the chart's title or subtitle already says what is plotted. A box with
36	one swatch restates the title and costs space.
37	
38	- **Label selectively - never a number on every point.** A value beside every dot or
39	  segment is chaos and goes unread. Label the endpoint, the extreme, or the one series
40	  the story is about; let the axis, the legend, and the tooltip/table carry the rest.
41	  Direct labels work *because* they are sparing - flood the chart and they stop working.
42	- **Direct labels before gridlines; gridlines before a second axis.**
43	- **A label that won't fit doesn't get clipped - measure first.** Only place a label
44	  *inside* a bar or stacked segment when the rendered text fits with comfortable
45	  padding on both sides. If it doesn't fit: for a whole bar/column, move the label
46	  outside the bar end (or to the tooltip if there's no room outside either); for an
47	  *interior* stacked segment (which has no free end),
48	  skip the inline label and let the legend + tooltip carry it. Either way the value
49	  stays in the table view, so nothing is gated. Never use `overflow: hidden` on the
50	  segment to "solve" it - that crops the first/last characters and is worse than no
51	  label. Text never overflows or is clipped by its own mark.
52	- Bars -> value at the tip. Columns -> value on the cap. Lines -> value at the end.
53	- Y-axis ticks: round to clean numbers (0 / 1,000 / 2,000), thousands-comma'd; they
54	  carry the values you didn't directly label, so keep them unless every value is labeled.
55	- **Text never wears the data color.** Marks - bars, lines, dots, area fills - carry
56	  the series color; labels, values, legends, and axis text use **text tokens**
57	  (primary / secondary / muted). A light categorical hue (yellow, aqua) is illegible
58	  as text on the surface. Identity comes from the colored mark *beside* the text - a
59	  dot, a short line-key, a swatch - never from coloring the text itself. A label set
60	  *inside* a colored fill (a stacked segment, a map tile) is the one exception: pick
61	  white or ink by the fill's luminance so it always clears contrast.
62	- **When end-labels collide, don't stack them.** Direct end-labels work when series
63	  separate at the right edge. When lines converge, nudging labels apart vertically
64	  detaches them from their lines and reads as noise - instead use **leader lines**
65	  (a thin connector from label to line-end), facet into **small multiples**, or fall
66	  back to the legend + tooltip. Past ~4 converging series, small multiples is usually right.
67	
68	## Figures - when the form is a number
69	
70	- **Stat tile** contract: `label` (sentence case, no trailing colon) · `value` (Sans
71	  semibold, auto-compact: 1,284 / 12.9K / $4.2M) · `delta` (optional; signed,
72	  vs a named period; color = direction × whether up is good) · `trend` (optional;
73	  12-point sparkline in the de-emphasis hue, current period in the accent).
74	- **Meter:** the fill carries severity (accent -> warning -> danger); the unfilled
75	  track is a **lighter step of the same ramp** (blue-on-blue, etc.) so state reads
76	  across the whole bar.
77	- **Hero figure.** The single number a dashboard leads with, >=48px, in the same
78	  sans as everything else (never a display or serif face - it reads as off-brand
79	  decoration). Exactly one per view.
80	- **Proportional figures for big numbers; tabular only in columns.** A large
81	  standalone value (hero figure, stat-tile value) uses the font's default
82	  proportional figures - `tabular-nums` gives every digit the width of a `0`, so a
83	  number like `121` looks loose at display sizes. Reserve
84	  `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns of numbers that must align
85	  vertically (table rows, axis ticks).
86	
87	## Texture - the backup channel (opt-in)
88	
89	Where hue fails - full-severity CVD, grayscale print, `forced-colors` - texture
90	carries identity. One directional hand-drawn fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror
91	only** (never horizontal/vertical - those read as gridlines/bars). Inked tone-on-tone
92	(a step from the fill's own ramp), equal loudness across slots. On value scales the
93	texture is *ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging
94	sign) so it never misstates the value. Triggered by an accessibility setting, print,
95	or `forced-colors` - never on by default. (See `palette.md`.)

"""Render uninsured_by_age.csv as a publication-quality line chart.

Reads uninsured_by_age.csv (year, age_group, pct_uninsured, margin_of_error)
and writes uninsured_by_age.png: one line per age group, shaded to show the
margin of error, with 2020 left as a genuine gap (no ACS 1-year data that
year) rather than interpolated across.
"""
import csv
from collections import defaultdict

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.font_manager as fm
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

CSV_PATH = "uninsured_by_age.csv"
PNG_PATH = "uninsured_by_age.png"

# Validated categorical palette (references/palette.md, slots 1-3 - this
# triple is the pre-validated all-pairs-safe subset for light mode).
COLORS = {
    "Under 19": "#2a78d6",     # slot 1, blue
    "19 to 64": "#eb6834",     # slot 2, orange
    "65 and over": "#1baf7a",  # slot 3, aqua
}
SERIES_ORDER = ["Under 19", "19 to 64", "65 and over"]

# Chart chrome & ink (references/palette.md, light mode)
SURFACE = "#fcfcfb"
INK_PRIMARY = "#0b0b0b"
INK_SECONDARY = "#52514e"
INK_MUTED = "#898781"
GRIDLINE = "#e1e0d9"
BASELINE = "#c3c2b7"

FULL_YEARS = list(range(2008, 2025))  # 2008..2024 inclusive


def load_data(path):
    data = defaultdict(dict)
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            yr = int(row["year"])
            data[row["age_group"]][yr] = (
                float(row["pct_uninsured"]),
                float(row["margin_of_error"]),
            )
    return data


def series_arrays(group_data):
    """Return x, pct, moe arrays over FULL_YEARS, with NaN for missing years
    (2020) so the line breaks there instead of interpolating across it."""
    xs, pct, moe = [], [], []
    for yr in FULL_YEARS:
        xs.append(yr)
        if yr in group_data:
            p, m = group_data[yr]
            pct.append(p)
            moe.append(m)
        else:
            pct.append(float("nan"))
            moe.append(float("nan"))
    return xs, pct, moe


def main():
    data = load_data(CSV_PATH)

    sans = [f.name for f in fm.fontManager.ttflist]
    family = "DejaVu Sans" if "DejaVu Sans" in sans else "sans-serif"
    plt.rcParams["font.family"] = family

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6), dpi=300)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)

    for group in SERIES_ORDER:
        xs, pct, moe = series_arrays(data[group])
        color = COLORS[group]
        lo = [p - m for p, m in zip(pct, moe)]
        hi = [p + m for p, m in zip(pct, moe)]

        # Margin-of-error band: series hue at ~10% opacity, a wash not a block.
        ax.fill_between(xs, lo, hi, color=color, alpha=0.10, linewidth=0, zorder=2)
        # Line: 2px, round join/cap.
        ax.plot(
            xs, pct, color=color, linewidth=2, solid_capstyle="round",
            solid_joinstyle="round", zorder=3,
        )

        # End marker with a surface-color ring, and a direct end label
        # (value only; text stays in ink, never the series color).
        last_yr = max(y for y in FULL_YEARS if y in data[group])
        last_val, _ = data[group][last_yr]
        ax.scatter(
            [last_yr], [last_val], s=64, color=color,
            edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=2, zorder=4,
        )
        ax.annotate(
            f"{group}\n{last_val:.1f}%",
            xy=(last_yr, last_val),
            xytext=(8, 0),
            textcoords="offset points",
            va="center",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=10,
            color=INK_SECONDARY,
            linespacing=1.3,
        )

    # 2020 gap annotation - explain the break rather than leaving it silent.
    ax.annotate(
        "2020 not collected\n(COVID-19)",
        xy=(2020, 1.0),
        xytext=(2020, -6),
        ha="center",
        va="top",
        fontsize=8.5,
        color=INK_MUTED,
        style="italic",
    )

    # Axes cosmetics: recessive hairline gridlines, muted ticks, no boxed frame.
    ax.set_ylim(-2, 26)
    ax.set_xlim(2007.3, 2027.5)
    ax.set_xticks(range(2008, 2025, 2))
    ax.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in range(2008, 2025, 2)], color=INK_MUTED, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_yticks(range(0, 26, 5))
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"{y}%" for y in range(0, 26, 5)], color=INK_MUTED, fontsize=10)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=GRIDLINE, linewidth=1, zorder=0)
    ax.xaxis.grid(False)
    for spine in ("top", "right", "left"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(BASELINE)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_linewidth(1)
    ax.tick_params(axis="both", length=0)

    # Title / subtitle (sentence case, primary/secondary ink).
    fig.text(0.06, 0.96, "Uninsured rate by age group, United States",
              fontsize=16, fontweight="bold", color=INK_PRIMARY, ha="left")
    fig.text(0.06, 0.915,
              "Percent of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with no health "
              "insurance coverage, 2008–2024, shaded band = 90% confidence margin of error",
              fontsize=10.5, color=INK_SECONDARY, ha="left")

    # Legend (always present for >=2 series), positioned above the plot.
    handles = [
        Line2D([0], [0], color=COLORS[g], linewidth=2, marker="o",
               markersize=6, markerfacecolor=COLORS[g], markeredgecolor=SURFACE,
               markeredgewidth=1.5)
        for g in SERIES_ORDER
    ]
    ax.legend(
        handles, SERIES_ORDER, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.0),
        frameon=False, fontsize=10, labelcolor=INK_SECONDARY, ncol=3,
        handlelength=1.6, columnspacing=1.4, borderaxespad=0,
    ).set_visible(False)  # end-of-line labels + swatch dots carry identity; avoid a redundant box

    # Source note.
    fig.text(
        0.06, 0.02,
        "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year estimates, "
        "2008–2024 (HIC-4/5/6_ACS historical tables). \"19 to 64\" and \"65 and over\" are "
        "derived from the published age groups; see SOURCES.md for method. Retrieved 2026-09-13.",
        fontsize=8, color=INK_MUTED, ha="left", wrap=True,
    )

    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.07, right=0.86, top=0.86, bottom=0.12)
    fig.savefig(PNG_PATH, facecolor=SURFACE)
    print(f"wrote {PNG_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Render uninsured_by_age.csv as a publication-quality figure that answers one
question: who gained coverage after the ACA's Marketplaces opened and Medicaid
expanded in January 2014?

Reads uninsured_by_age.csv (year, age_group, pct_uninsured, margin_of_error)
and writes uninsured_by_age.png. Marks January 2014, shades the 2013-2016
window, and labels each group's percentage-point change over that window.
2020 is left as a genuine gap (no ACS 1-year data that year) rather than
interpolated across.
"""
import csv
from collections import defaultdict

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.font_manager as fm
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

CSV_PATH = "uninsured_by_age.csv"
PNG_PATH = "uninsured_by_age.png"

# Validated categorical palette (references/palette.md, slots 1-3 - this
# triple is the pre-validated all-pairs-safe subset for light mode).
COLORS = {
    "Under 19": "#2a78d6",     # slot 1, blue
    "19 to 64": "#eb6834",     # slot 2, orange
    "65 and over": "#1baf7a",  # slot 3, aqua
}
SERIES_ORDER = ["Under 19", "19 to 64", "65 and over"]

# Chart chrome & ink (references/palette.md, light mode)
SURFACE = "#fcfcfb"
INK_PRIMARY = "#0b0b0b"
INK_SECONDARY = "#52514e"
INK_MUTED = "#898781"
GRIDLINE = "#e1e0d9"
BASELINE = "#c3c2b7"
BAND_TINT = "#ece9e2"  # neutral wash marking the 2013-2016 window

FULL_YEARS = list(range(2008, 2025))  # 2008..2024 inclusive

# Where each series' delta callout is anchored (data coords), chosen to sit
# in the clear vertical gap between that series' band and its neighbor's.
DELTA_LABEL_Y = {
    "19 to 64": 17.0,
    "Under 19": 9.0,
    "65 and over": 3.2,
}


def load_data(path):
    data = defaultdict(dict)
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            yr = int(row["year"])
            data[row["age_group"]][yr] = (
                float(row["pct_uninsured"]),
                float(row["margin_of_error"]),
            )
    return data


def series_arrays(group_data):
    """Return x, pct, moe arrays over FULL_YEARS, with NaN for missing years
    (2020) so the line breaks there instead of interpolating across it."""
    xs, pct, moe = [], [], []
    for yr in FULL_YEARS:
        xs.append(yr)
        if yr in group_data:
            p, m = group_data[yr]
            pct.append(p)
            moe.append(m)
        else:
            pct.append(float("nan"))
            moe.append(float("nan"))
    return xs, pct, moe


def main():
    data = load_data(CSV_PATH)

    sans = [f.name for f in fm.fontManager.ttflist]
    family = "DejaVu Sans" if "DejaVu Sans" in sans else "sans-serif"
    plt.rcParams["font.family"] = family

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6.4), dpi=300)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)

    # Shaded window marking when Marketplace and expanded-Medicaid coverage
    # took effect, drawn first so every data layer sits on top of it.
    ax.axvspan(2013, 2016, color=BAND_TINT, zorder=0, linewidth=0)

    for group in SERIES_ORDER:
        xs, pct, moe = series_arrays(data[group])
        color = COLORS[group]
        lo = [p - m for p, m in zip(pct, moe)]
        hi = [p + m for p, m in zip(pct, moe)]

        # Margin-of-error band: series hue at ~10% opacity, a wash not a block.
        ax.fill_between(xs, lo, hi, color=color, alpha=0.10, linewidth=0, zorder=2)
        # Line: 2px, round join/cap.
        ax.plot(
            xs, pct, color=color, linewidth=2, solid_capstyle="round",
            solid_joinstyle="round", zorder=3,
        )

        # Anchor markers at the two points being compared, 2013 and 2016.
        v2013, _ = data[group][2013]
        v2016, _ = data[group][2016]
        ax.scatter(
            [2013, 2016], [v2013, v2016], s=46, color=color,
            edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.5, zorder=4,
        )

        # Delta callout: bold value in ink (never the series color) with a
        # small colored dot for identity, connected to the 2016 point by a
        # thin leader line.
        delta = v2016 - v2013
        label_y = DELTA_LABEL_Y[group]
        label_x = 2016.6
        ax.annotate(
            "",
            xy=(2016, v2016), xycoords="data",
            xytext=(label_x, label_y), textcoords="data",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK_MUTED, linewidth=0.8,
                             shrinkA=0, shrinkB=5),
            zorder=3,
        )
        ax.scatter([label_x], [label_y], s=26, color=color, zorder=5,
                   edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1)
        ax.text(
            label_x + 0.35, label_y,
            f"{group}: {delta:+.1f} pts",
            fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", color=INK_PRIMARY,
            va="center", ha="left", zorder=5,
        )

    # January 2014: solid line for a real event (vs. the dashed line used
    # below for a data gap).
    ax.axvline(2014, color=INK_SECONDARY, linewidth=1.2, zorder=1)
    ax.annotate(
        "Marketplaces open,\nMedicaid expansion\ntakes effect — Jan 2014",
        xy=(2014, 24.6), xytext=(2013.75, 24.6),
        ha="right", va="top", fontsize=8.5, color=INK_SECONDARY,
        linespacing=1.4,
    )

    # 2020 gap: a dashed guide line, labeled small so it stays secondary to
    # the 2014 story.
    ax.axvline(2020, color=BASELINE, linewidth=1, linestyle=(0, (3, 2)), zorder=1)
    ax.annotate(
        "2020: ACS data\nnot collected",
        xy=(2020, 24.6), xytext=(2020.25, 24.6),
        ha="left", va="top", fontsize=8, color=INK_MUTED, style="italic",
        linespacing=1.3,
    )

    # Axes cosmetics: recessive hairline gridlines, muted ticks, no boxed frame.
    ax.set_ylim(-2, 26)
    ax.set_xlim(2007.3, 2024.9)
    ax.set_xticks(range(2008, 2025, 2))
    ax.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in range(2008, 2025, 2)], color=INK_MUTED, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_yticks(range(0, 26, 5))
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"{y}%" for y in range(0, 26, 5)], color=INK_MUTED, fontsize=10)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=GRIDLINE, linewidth=1, zorder=0.5)
    ax.xaxis.grid(False)
    for spine in ("top", "right", "left"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(BASELINE)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_linewidth(1)
    ax.tick_params(axis="both", length=0)

    # Title / subtitle (sentence case, primary/secondary ink). Two short,
    # manually-broken lines rather than relying on auto-wrap, so nothing
    # runs past the figure edge.
    fig.text(0.06, 0.965,
              "Working-age adults gained the most coverage after 2014",
              fontsize=17, fontweight="bold", color=INK_PRIMARY, ha="left", va="top")
    fig.text(0.06, 0.918,
              "Uninsured rate by age group, United States, 2008–2024. Labels show the\n"
              "percentage-point change from 2013 to 2016, when ACA Marketplace and Medicaid-\n"
              "expansion coverage took effect. Shaded band = 90% confidence margin of error.",
              fontsize=10.5, color=INK_SECONDARY, ha="left", va="top", linespacing=1.5)

    # Legend (always present for >=2 series) - the dependable identity channel.
    handles = [
        Line2D([0], [0], color=COLORS[g], linewidth=2, marker="o",
               markersize=6, markerfacecolor=COLORS[g], markeredgecolor=SURFACE,
               markeredgewidth=1.5)
        for g in SERIES_ORDER
    ]
    fig.legend(
        handles, SERIES_ORDER, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.06, 0.80),
        frameon=False, fontsize=10, labelcolor=INK_SECONDARY, ncol=3,
        handlelength=1.6, columnspacing=1.4, borderaxespad=0,
    )

    # Source note.
    fig.text(
        0.06, 0.02,
        "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year estimates, "
        "2008–2024 (HIC-4/5/6_ACS historical tables). \"19 to 64\" and \"65 and over\" are\n"
        "derived from the published age groups; see SOURCES.md for method. Retrieved 2026-09-13.",
        fontsize=8, color=INK_MUTED, ha="left", linespacing=1.5,
    )

    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.07, right=0.98, top=0.75, bottom=0.12)
    fig.savefig(PNG_PATH, facecolor=SURFACE)
    print(f"wrote {PNG_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
